name: AlNahla Group | مجموعة النهلة
note: Gate 2/Gate 6: diversified Jeddah holding (investment/real estate/SAMACO automotive/SAMACO Marine yachts/hospitality). Its trading cluster is wholesale (SAMACO Toys distributes to ToysRus, SACO, Carrefour etc., not its own stores) plus marine dealerships; the holding site has no storefront and no substantial dedicated consumer retail arm.

name: NANCO Group
note: Gate 2 category: ground transport, fuel-station services and airport services since 1969. Logistics/services business, an explicit hard-fail category, not retail.

name: مفارش العييري
note: Held resolved in favor: independent check confirms a broad multi-line home-textiles retailer (bedding, comforters, sheets, pillows, felt, sleeping supplies; 8+ categories), physical stores in Dammam and Buraydah, live Salla store plus iOS/Android apps, active discount codes and Kingdom-wide shipping. Not mattress-only; broad soft-goods with seasonal/gifting repeat purchase passes Gate 3, and multi-store + apps + broad catalog satisfies Gate 5a.

name: Ali Zaid Al-Quraishi & Brothers
note: Gate 2/Gate 6 category: 1958 diversified family holding whose consumer-goods line is brand marketing/distribution, alongside automotive, supply chain, industrial, real estate and financial services. Corporate 'investment company' site with no storefront and no dedicated retail arm of its own.

name: AlRashed Building Materials Co.
note: Gate 2 category: construction building-materials supplier (sections, sheets, pipes, rebar, wood panels) serving contractors via 30+ branches. Explicit construction-materials hard-fail regardless of scale.

name: Al Rashed Tires
note: Gate 2 category: OTR/industrial tire and battery distributor targeting dealers, fleets and OEMs via a B2B registration model. Automotive tires/batteries are an explicit hard-fail category.

name: Al Rawabi Group of Companies W.L.L
note: Gate 6: alrawabigroup.com is the conglomerate holding page mixing retail with wholesale (Wholesale Plus/Emdadco), food manufacturing, distribution and hospitality. The genuine hypermarket storefront sits on a separate domain (rawabihypermarket.com) already captured as its own row, so the mixed-parent holding page is correctly excluded (no double-count).

name: ALSAIF Trading Agencies Co.
note: Gate 2 corrected clause: live-fetch confirms Al Saif Company is a manufacturer/distributor selling through 1,300+ distributors and third-party hypermarkets/e-stores, directing consumers to 'find the nearest distributor' with no own cart (the alsaifco.sa micro-store is loyalty-redemption only). No substantial dedicated retail arm; matches the Alireza Holding fail pattern. Distinct from the separate 73-store Alsaif Gallery retailer on alsaifgallery.com.

name: AlSaif Group
note: Gate 2 category: transportation, logistics and real-estate conglomerate (est. 1960) with no consumer products sold. Hard-fail non-retail category.

name: Mohamed Naser Al-Sayer & Sons Establishment Company W.L.L.
note: Gate 2/Gate 6 category: Kuwait's largest Toyota/Lexus automotive distributor and automotive-led diversified conglomerate; alsayeronline.com is the automotive portal. Automotive dealer/distributor is an explicit hard-fail category.

name: Marzooq S. Al Shamlan Holding
note: Gate 6: mixed Qatari conglomerate blending automotive (Q-Tire tires/batteries) and B2B garage/cleaning equipment (QTC) with a separate 19-boutique watch-retail arm (Crono/Watch Corner). The holding domain is a corporate page with no cart; the mixed parent is correctly excluded and the watch-retail subsidiary would be its own separate entity/row.

name: Alshareef for building materials
note: Gate 2 category: B2B building-materials importer (bricks, rebar, timber) since 1975. Explicit construction-materials hard-fail category.

name: Alsourayia Trading Co.
note: Gate 3 narrow-category: verified as السريع للأرضيات, Saudi's leading flooring/carpet retailer (vinyl, laminate, LVT, carpets/rugs, carpet tiles, artificial grass, mosque carpets). Flooring/carpet only is an explicitly confirmed narrow, low-repeat fail pattern.

name: IKEA Alsulaiman
note: Gates 1-5 pass: the account name is the IKEA retail brand itself, a genuine substantial Saudi-operated franchise (Ghassan Alsulaiman Furniture Trading Co., exclusive IKEA franchise since 1983, 11+ in-Kingdom stores, full live e-commerce on ikea.com/sa with Mada/Apple Pay/Tamara/Tabby/Al Rajhi installments/same-day delivery). The Gate 6 exclusion nitpicked the holding domain, but this account represents the qualifying retail subsidiary the ICP says to evaluate on its own merits, with no duplicate ikea.com/sa row to consolidate against.

name: السلطان | AlSultan
note: Gate 3 pass: not a single narrow line but a multi-category home-textiles retailer (bedroom textiles, summer/winter bedspreads, pillows, mattress toppers, plus bathroom textiles, bathrobes, prayer mats, shawls, fragrances; 8 categories), live Salla store since 1981 with shipping/tracking and promo codes. Bed linens/towels refresh seasonally and are heavily gifted, so the flooring/carpet-only analogy is inapt; broad soft-goods scale satisfies Gate 5a.

name: ALTAWKILAT
note: Gate 2 category: major Saudi automotive distributor (Maserati, Infiniti, Chevrolet, GMC, Dongfeng, Hongqi) under Tawad Holding. Explicit automotive hard-fail, and the domain is currently a parked Bitly redirect.

name: Al Waha For Cars
note: Gate 2 category: Qatar Jetour car dealership (showrooms, cars for sale/rent, service centers). Explicit automotive hard-fail category.

name: Al Wajba Motors
note: Gate 2 category: exclusive Qatar dealer for Bentley, Lamborghini, Bugatti and McLaren. Explicit luxury-automotive hard-fail category.

name: Al Wazzan Group of Companies
note: Gate 6/Gate 4: Kuwaiti diversified holding (real estate, healthcare, automotive/Ford, retail-distribution, construction); the site is a defunct placeholder (returns 503) with no storefront of its own. Mixed-conglomerate parent with no live retail; any retail vertical would be a separate subsidiary.

name: Alwazzan United Trading company
note: Gate 3/Gate 4: Kuwait home fit-out firm (bespoke kitchens, built-in wardrobes, doors, luxury safes) on an appointment/consultation basis with no cart or pricing ('Book an Appointment' only). One-time project-based fixtures are low-repeat, matching the narrow-fail pattern, and it lacks a real transactional channel.

name: شركة اليحيا Alyahya Company
note: Gate 2 category: thin dated (2011) corporate site listing Cars, Automotive Service, Spare Parts, Apiaries, Nurseries and Realty. Automotive and real estate are hard-fail and apiaries/nurseries are agriculture; no qualifying retail category or storefront.

name: Alymama اليمامة
note: Gate 3/Gate 5: a genuine small Riyadh e-commerce store but the entire catalog is ~20 watch color-variants plus 3 belts, a single narrow low-repeat accessory line that also falls well below the ~50-SKU Gate 5a substantiality floor.

name: Hassan Misfer Al-Zahrani & Partners Group
note: Gate 2 category: Al Zahrani Holding is an industrial/trading conglomerate (trading, contracting, cargo, travel, stainless-steel fabrication, industrial maintenance). None are qualifying retail categories and the legacy site has no storefront.

name: Amazon KSA Markets
note: Gate 1 geography: the operating entity is Amazon.com Inc., globally HQ'd in Seattle, USA, so it fails in-country HQ regardless of substantial KSA operations. The official KSA store is also amazon.sa, not this anti-bot-challenge domain.
